payload.title: tool_health classifies every precision feedback row whose source_type is not ai_judge or ai_consensus as human_judged, so outcome and canary rows add to human_judged_samples and make a tool read human_judged or mixed_judged in the operator_judged_precision that readiness reports
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tool_health.py:684-688 (source_type ai_consensus is counted apart; ai_judge is skipped; every other value, outcome and canary included, increments human_judged)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tool_health.py:757-768 (_precision_status turns a non-zero human_judged into human_judged or mixed_judged)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback_store.py:154 (FEEDBACK_SOURCE_TYPES lists human, ai_judge, ai_consensus, outcome and canary)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/readiness.py:179 (operator_judged_precision is the precision whenever the status is human_judged or mixed_judged)
payload.rule_violated: CLAUDE.md one owner per concept: the set of source types that count as a person is decided once (feedback_store source types), not by exclusion at one reader
payload.notes: An outcome row (minted by outcome_truth from a merged change) or a canary row (a planted item, true by construction) is a kernel-written label, not an operator judgment. tool_health tests only for ai_consensus and ai_judge, so both land in the else branch and are counted as human_judged, and readiness then publishes the precision as operator_judged_precision. Latent today: the audit found no outcome rows and the canary corpus is never registered, so the miscount appears the day either lane produces rows. Close condition: Classify the source type by an explicit allow-list (human only counts as human_judged; outcome and canary count in their own buckets), and a test feeds one outcome row and one canary row for a tool and asserts human_judged_samples stays 0 and operator_judged_precision is None. Verified at origin/main d716541239.
